    SieveOfAtkin(int n)
    Sieve of Atkin algorithm finds all prime numbers up to a given limit n It is s an optimization that uses quadratic formulas (based on modulo 12 properties) to mark prime candidates, and then eliminates multiples of prime squares It prints the first 3 and last 2 primes along with execution time.

    SieveOfSundaram(int n)
    Sieve of Sundaram algorithm finds all prime numbers up to a given limit n It works by eliminating numbers 'k' of the form i + j + 2ij Numbers 'i' that are not eliminated are used to find primes using the formula 2*i + 1.     • CalculatePrimeNumbers

      public static void CalculatePrimeNumbers()
      Function takes an integer that equal/larger than 12 from the user. Calculates primes to n by using Sieve of Eratosthenes, Sieve of Sundaram, and Sieve of Atkin algorithms. Shows the execution time to compare.

    • SieveOfEratosthenes

      public static void SieveOfEratosthenes(int n)
      Sieve of Eratosthenes algorithm finds all prime numbers up to a given limit n. It iteratively marks multiples of each prime number starting from 2 as not prime It prints the first 3 and last 2 primes along with execution time.
      Parameters:
      n - The upper limit for prime number generation.

    • SieveOfSundaram

      public static void SieveOfSundaram(int n)
      Sieve of Sundaram algorithm finds all prime numbers up to a given limit n It works by eliminating numbers 'k' of the form i + j + 2ij Numbers 'i' that are not eliminated are used to find primes using the formula 2*i + 1. (2 is added manually) It prints the first 3 and last 2 primes along with execution time
      Parameters:
      n - is the upper limit for prime number generation

    • SieveOfAtkin

      public static void SieveOfAtkin(int n)
      Sieve of Atkin algorithm finds all prime numbers up to a given limit n It is s an optimization that uses quadratic formulas (based on modulo 12 properties) to mark prime candidates, and then eliminates multiples of prime squares It prints the first 3 and last 2 primes along with execution time.
      Parameters:
      n - is the upper limit for prime number generation.

    • calculateManhattanDistance

      public static double calculateManhattanDistance(int[] a, int[] b)
      Calculates the Manhattan Distance between two arrays. Formula: |a1 - b1| + |a2 - b2| + ... + |an - bn|
      Parameters:
      a - First integer array.
      b - Second integer array.
      Returns:
      The total Manhattan Distance as a double value.

    • calculateEuclideanDistance

      public static double calculateEuclideanDistance(int[] a, int[] b)
      Calculates the Euclidean Distance between two arrays. Formula: √((a1 - b1)² + (a2 - b2)² + ... + (an - bn)²)
      Parameters:
      a - First integer array.
      b - Second integer array.
      Returns:
      The Euclidean Distance as a double value.

    • calculateCosineSimilarity

      public static double calculateCosineSimilarity(int[] a, int[] b)
      It calculates the Cosine Similarity between two arrays. Formula: (A · B) / (|A| × |B|) It shows how similar the two arrays are in direction (not magnitude).
      Parameters:
      a - first integer array
      b - second integer array
      Returns:
      The Cosine Similarity value in range [0, 1]. Returns 0 if a or b is a zero vector.
